news_posts.post_content:
Too many banks are deploying AI chat agents without a clear governance framework.
The recent WIRED story shows several institutions pulling back after agents gave inconsistent advice,
causing compliance headaches.

Governance means setting rules for model selection,
 data quality,
 testing,
 and ongoing monitoring.
Think of it as a checklist that lives alongside any new software release.

A practical framework:

1. Define the scope – what questions the agent may answer.

2. Choose a model that meets regulatory standards for explainability.

3. Build a test suite with real‑world banking queries and edge cases.

4. Set up continuous monitoring for drift,
 bias,
 and error rates.

5. Require human sign‑off before any change goes live.

These steps separate fact from guesswork.
The fact: unchecked agents can produce misleading information,
 as reported by WIRED.
Interpretation: a governance layer prevents costly retractions and protects customers.

Start by drafting a simple governance checklist for any AI pilot.
If you already have one, review it this week and add a monitoring clause.
A disciplined approach turns a risky experiment into a reliable service.
